nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Light drives growth of the oaks, heath and gorse that cover the slopes and valleys of the site.

nodes.name: Atlantic rainfall
nodes.desc: Mountains block moist Atlantic air, giving very heavy rain, roughly 1,600 mm a year low down and about 3,200 mm on the heights.

nodes.name: Clear mountain streams
nodes.desc: Cold, fast, clean streams drain the granite uplands and support trout, otters and the rare Pyrenean desman.

nodes.name: Mountain soil and litter
nodes.desc: Thin soils and leaf litter hold the nutrients that oak woods, heath and bilberry draw back up.

nodes.name: Fungi and bacteria
nodes.desc: Break down fallen leaves, carcasses and dung, returning nutrients to the soil and streams.

nodes.name: Pedunculate oak
nodes.desc: One of the oaks that dominate the broadleaf woods of the valleys. Its acorns and leaves feed boar and roe deer.

nodes.name: Heather
nodes.desc: Dwarf shrub of the heath that makes up much of the shrubland, with gorse. Browsed by roe deer and grazers.

nodes.name: Bilberry
nodes.desc: Low berry shrub of the upland woods and heath. Its leaves and fruit are eaten by roe deer and foxes.

nodes.name: Dwarf gorse
nodes.desc: Spiny evergreen shrub that, with heather, dominates the shrublands covering most of the site.

nodes.name: Rusty willow
nodes.desc: Streamside willow whose leaves fall into the water and feed stream insects.

nodes.name: Roe deer
nodes.desc: Small deer, abundant around the park margins and a symbol of the site. Feeds on shoots, leaves and berries.

nodes.name: Wild boar
nodes.desc: Omnivore that digs roots and eats acorns, berries, small animals and carrion. A main prey of the wolf.

nodes.name: Spanish ibex
nodes.desc: Wild goat that returned to the mountains after the Gerês ibex died out in the 1890s; about 100 animals by 2011.

nodes.name: Garrano horse
nodes.desc: Small semi-feral mountain horse, present across about 97% of the park, living in harems on the high plateaus.

nodes.name: Stream insect larvae
nodes.desc: Caddisfly and similar larvae shred fallen leaves in the streams; the main food of the Pyrenean desman.

nodes.name: Pyrenean desman
nodes.desc: Small aquatic mole that hunts stream insect larvae, mostly. Vulnerable in Portugal and a sign of clean water.

nodes.name: Brown trout
nodes.desc: Fish of the park rivers, eating stream insects. Native fish are the preferred food of otters in Iberia.

nodes.name: Eurasian otter
nodes.desc: Well adapted to the park waters. Eats mainly fish, plus amphibians and sometimes the desman.

nodes.name: Iberian frog
nodes.desc: Frog of cool mountain streams, catching small invertebrates; widely eaten by snakes, birds and mammals.

nodes.name: Red fox
nodes.desc: Opportunist that takes small animals and berries and scavenges carcasses.

nodes.name: Common genet
nodes.desc: Slender nocturnal carnivore that hunts amphibians, reptiles, birds and small mammals.

nodes.name: Common buzzard
nodes.desc: Raptor that hunts small animals and also takes carrion.

nodes.name: Iberian wolf
nodes.desc: Top predator, now rare in the park. In the Iberian mountains boar and roe deer are its main prey.
